historical_spelling: sar, sare, sarre, sær, sore, zore, soir, sair
job: intensifier: severely, greatly, painfully (adverb); painful, grievous, severe (adjective)
definition: Adverb: so as to cause considerable physical pain or injury; severely, grievously; greatly, deeply (OED sore adv.). Adjective: causing or involving pain or distress; in intensive use very great or serious (OED sore adj.1).
usage_notes: Patterns (OED): after a verb of striking or hurting, OE-ModE: OE "Þonne he hi sare sloh" (Anglo-Saxon Psalter lxxvii. 33); after a verb of grieving, OE-ModE: OE "Me þæt cynn hafað sare abolgen." (Genesis 1257); before a participle or adjective of distress, ME-ModE: c1175 "sare offdredde" (Ormulum l. 3809); full sore, ME-EME: c1320 "Fulle sore mowe heo then dreden." (Castle of Love 1580); comparative and superlative, ME-ModE: 1340 "Huo þet heȝest ualþ þe zorer he him blecheþ." (Ayenbite 238); to sit one sore, ME-EME (obsolete c1420-1560): c1420 "That sittus me nowe fulle sore." (Sir Amadace xxi); lay sore upon, EME: 1611 "because shee lay sore vpon him" (KJV Judges xiv. 17; only quotation found); before a noun, OE-ModE: OE "Nu þu ealle forlæt sare sorgceare." (Crist I 209); latest 1892 "a sore temptation" (Photography Annual vol. II. 893). Now chiefly archaic and dialect.
quote: Swa hyt lungre wearð on hyra sincgifan sare geendod.
source: Oxford English Dictionary, sore adv., sense 5.a (quotation from Beowulf)
